cards.text: Grab your apron, friend. The Jewish Passover is near, and Jesus goes up to Jerusalem. Fair warning, this is NOT a quiet trip, so keep your hands and mustaches inside the ride at ALL times.
He walks into the temple courts and finds men selling animals, and money changers seated at their tables. It's a livestock auction and a bank lobby. In the SAME room.

cards.question: In the temple courts, men are selling cattle, sheep and ___.

cards.text: Now watch what Jesus does. He doesn't ask to speak to the manager. He takes some cords and makes something out of them.

cards.question: What does Jesus make out of cords in the temple courts?
When Jesus drives everyone out of the temple courts, the sheep and cattle go too.
What does Jesus do to the money changers and their tables?

answers.text: He pours out their coins and overturns the tables
He carries their tables out to the street
He gathers their coins and folds up the tables

cards.text: Coins rolling EVERYWHERE. Then Jesus turns to the men selling doves: "Get these out of here!" That is NOT a suggestion, friend.

cards.question: Jesus tells the dove sellers they've turned His Father's house into a ___.

cards.text: His disciples are watching all of this, and they remember something that is written in Scripture. Me? Something wild happens and the only thing I remember is that I left the oven on.

cards.question: What is the Scripture the disciples remember about?

cards.text: After all this, the Jews there have a demand for Jesus. And it is NOT "Can we help you pick up the coins?"

cards.question: What do the Jews demand that Jesus show them?

answers.text: A sign to prove His authority
A letter from the high priest
A record of His family line

cards.text: Here's Jesus' answer, and you might want to sit down for this one: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again."
The Jews fire right back. This temple took forty-six YEARS to build, they say, and He's going to raise it up in three days?

cards.question: When the Jews hear Jesus' answer, they think raising this temple up in three days sounds easy.

cards.text: They're counting the building in their heads, stone by stone. But HERE'S the twist, friend: Jesus was speaking about a different temple.

cards.question: What temple was Jesus speaking about?
When do the disciples remember that Jesus said this about the temple?

answers.text: After He was raised from the dead
On the walk back to Galilee
At the very next Passover Feast

cards.text: Then they believe the Scripture and the word Jesus had spoken. Some words only click LATER, like a recipe I read on Monday that finally makes sense on Thursday, halfway through the batch.
Now we're back at the Passover Feast in Jerusalem, and Jesus is doing signs. People are watching like it's the last ten seconds of a tied game.

cards.question: Many people see the signs Jesus is doing and ___ in His name.
Jesus entrusts Himself to the people at the feast who believe in His name.
Why doesn't Jesus entrust Himself to the people at the feast?

cards.text: Nobody has to tell Jesus what people are like, because He knew what was in a man. Me? I can't even tell what's in a cookie box until I open the lid.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "He walks into the temple courts and finds men selling animals, and money changers seated at their tables." / "It's a livestock auction and a bank lobby." / "In the SAME room."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Now watch what Jesus does." / "He doesn't ask to speak to the manager." / "He takes some cords and makes something out of them."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus "drives everyone out." John 2:15 says He "drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle." The text doesn't say whether "all" includes the people or only the animals. "Everyone" decides a point the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Coins rolling EVERYWHERE." / "Then Jesus turns to the men selling doves: 'Get these out of here!'" / "That is NOT a suggestion, friend."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "Coins rolling EVERYWHERE" is told as narration, not as a joke, and it goes further than John 2:15, which says only that He poured out the coins of the money changers.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "His disciples are watching all of this, and they remember something that is written in Scripture." / "Me?" / "Something wild happens and the only thing I remember is that I left the oven on."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No card ever tells the Scripture the disciples remember: "Zeal for Your house will consume Me" (John 2:17). Card 11 only asks what it is about, "Zeal for God's house," and the stop then ends. The baker never learns the "will consume Me" part, which links the line to Jesus.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 4 has just told the Jews' disbelieving reply ("forty-six YEARS... and He's going to raise it up in three days?"). This true or false card then asks whether they think it sounds easy. The baker only repeats what they just read, so the card adds nothing to their understanding. It also tests what the Jews think, which the text doesn't state.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: "They're counting the building in their heads, stone by stone" states what the Jews are thinking as fact. John 2:20 gives only their words, and the line isn't marked as Papa Dorin's guess.

rule.text: Feelings: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
